newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 15.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Thursday:

- Police have taken possession of files held by the managing director of a finance company which is being investigated due to irregularities. The Irish Mortgage and Finance Bureau, Limerick, was closed yesterday.
- Nearly all of Ireland's 23 independent radio stations are now profitable and are posing a challenge for national advertising.
- Pro-Life groups plan to lobby Fianna Fail, which heads a minority Irish government, to hold an abortion referendum within two years

- Andy McCarter is to take over the running of the Irish operation of Fruit of the Loom. He is a brother of the company's Irish chief executive, Wille McCarter, who is threatened with redundancy by the U.S. parent company.
- Effluent has wiped out eight miles of the river Mulkear in Limericak, the third major fish kill this summer
- Police are investigating financial irregularities at a Limerick mortgage brokerage which has closedits offices. Initial estimates are that 300,000 Irish pounds is unaccounted for.
